_TEMPLATE_NOTE: This is the EXAMPLE config. Copy it to config.json and edit, or run the 'setup-news-digest' skill to generate config.json from your answers. The digest folder is resolved dynamically by the _pipeline scripts, so it is intentionally NOT stored here.
_comment: Single source of truth for the daily-news-digest orchestrator. Edit here, not in the task prompt. The digest folder is resolved dynamically by the _pipeline scripts (--folder > $DAILY_NEWS_FOLDER > parent of _pipeline/), so it is intentionally NOT stored here.
_digest_title_comment: Branding shown in the HTML <title> and header. The last word is styled in an accent color. Set this to whatever you like (e.g. "Alex's Morning Brief"). The setup-news-digest skill fills this in for you.
_dedup_inject_cap_comment: Max number of most-recent dedup entries injected into each topic agent's prompt (token saver). The FULL 30-day history is still checked deterministically post-selection by intake_candidates.py, so capping the injected list does not weaken dedup. 0 or negative = no cap.

figures._comment: Optional data figures in story cards. OFF by default; leave it off unless you want them. 'chart' figures are generated locally as inline HTML/SVG from numbers the story already cites -- no network at read time, no third-party package, no licensing question. Enable per topic with the topic's "figures" field ("none" or "chart"). Most days should still produce none.

chart._aspect_comment: Width:height of the line chart's coordinate space. Editorial, not layout: a wide short chart flattens slopes, a taller one exaggerates them. The chart always renders at 100% of the card width regardless.

topics.definition: Major international developments — conflicts, diplomacy, elections, and cross-border events with global significance. Prefer consequential shifts over routine updates.

Federal and state legislation, court rulings, elections, and regulatory changes in the United States. Anchor to what actually changes for people and institutions. This topic uses the optional 'State Watch' angle below to add a local read for the markets/states you follow.
Structural technology developments: major platform and product shifts, AI milestones, cybersecurity, and significant research breakthroughs. Not routine product updates.
Markets and macroeconomics, corporate finance, major M&A, earnings that move a sector, and notable fraud/enforcement. Anchor to what it means for the broader economy.
Research discoveries and genuine milestones across the sciences — new findings, published results, and mission outcomes. Prefer findings over hype.

wildcard._comment: Daily Wild Card: ONE serendipity pick from the top financial headlines of the last 24 hours. Gathered by a 6th parallel agent, selected by the orchestrator weighted by the 👍/👎 history in news_feedback.md (Liked stories = pull toward, Active preferences = push away). Additive like On Your Radar — never counts toward story_count min/max. Set enabled=false to drop the card without touching the task prompt.
wildcard.definition: The single most consequential or genuinely surprising financial story of the last 24 hours: markets (equities, bonds, FX, commodities), Fed/macro, banking, corporate finance, major M&A, IPOs, earnings that move a sector, sovereign debt, notable fraud/enforcement. EXCLUDED: anything a core topic agent already owns (e.g. Business & Markets, Technology) — the wild card must come from outside your configured beats.

_focus_state_tags_comment: Optional short labels for the State Watch pill, mapping each focus_states entry to the tag rendered in the digest (and offered to agents in the return schema). Omit an entry to use its full name. Not US-specific -- use whatever short form suits your regions.
_focus_state_markets_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY, used by the 'US Politics & Policy' topic (enrichment: state-watch). List the states you want a local read on and, for each, the specific city/county markets you follow. Replace these examples with your own, or set both this and focus_states empty and switch that topic's enrichment to 'regional+divergence' if you don't want a local angle.
official_sources: The New York Times (paywalled — headlines/excerpts only)

source_screen._comment: Used by intake_candidates.py to structurally flag weak sourcing. aggregator_denylist = domains that are content aggregators / SEO-listicle / price-prediction hubs, not journalism. primary_domain_hints = substrings that mark a primary source (institution/regulator/paper). dedup_similarity_threshold = core_topic/headline TEXT similarity at/above which two candidates are flagged as possible duplicates for the model to adjudicate.
source_screen._event_key_comment: Event-key / entity check (intake_candidates.py) — catches 'same underlying report, different framing,' which pure text similarity misses because reframing tanks the difflib/Jaccard score. In addition to the text threshold above, two candidates (or a candidate vs. a history entry) are flagged as a possible duplicate when they share a distinctive event key: a cited article URL, or a high-containment overlap of named entities + salient numbers. entity_similarity_threshold = |shared entities| / min(sig sizes) at/above which the entity path fires; min_shared_entities = absolute count of shared entities also required, so tiny incidental overlaps don't trip it; min_entities_for_check = both signatures must have at least this many entities before the entity path is even considered. All hits are FLAGGED for the model to adjudicate, never auto-merged.

_agent_candidates_per_topic_comment: How many candidates each topic agent returns. The wild card uses wildcard.count instead. Raise for more choice at triage, lower to cut tokens.

agent_retry._comment: In-run recovery for transient agent failures (529/429/timeout/malformed JSON). max_retries = re-launches per failed agent before dropping its topic; the retry prompt tells the agent to use the reduced budget below so a blip retry stays cheap.

_framing_check_categories_comment: Categories whose recent dedup headlines are returned verbatim to the orchestrator (framing_ground_truth in the --emit-agent-prompts summary) for the framing-consistency check on ongoing-conflict stories.
_state_keep_days_comment: checkpoint.py clean removes _pipeline/state/<date>/ dirs older than this many days (Phase 4 hygiene).
_digest_timezone_comment: IANA timezone for all times in story bodies and framing (e.g. America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo). build_context.py injects it into every agent prompt (__TIMEZONE__ in briefing/main.md): agents convert UTC event times (geomagnetic storm peaks, economic data releases, etc.) to this zone with the correct seasonal abbreviation. Never leave a UTC timestamp as the only time reference.
